quotes.text: Power Automate executes rules. Copilot Studio interprets intention. Together, they are the difference between a rigid macro and a responsive assistant.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the division of labour between deterministic flows and a reasoning agent.

quotes.text: Automation without reasoning is dumb speed. Automation with reasoning becomes adaptive intelligence. Most people approach automation backward. They start with tools, then wonder why the workflow still feels robotic.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable thesis on why reasoning must come before tools.

quotes.text: Instructions versus tools, instructions are logic, tools are execution. Instructions tell it what kind of agent it is, tools tell it how to do what it claims to do.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly separates agent instructions from agent capabilities.

quotes.text: Those text fields you ignored while adding tools, they are the prompts, the model reads, when choosing what to do.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why tool descriptions drive the agent's tool selection.

quotes.text: When you need a deterministic flow, say, whenever a form response arrives, create a task, that's power-automate territory. When you need interpretive flexibility, like add whatever tasks came up in today's meeting, that's Co-pilot's domain.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a practical rule for choosing between a flow and an agent.

From task juggler to task commander

takeaways: A Copilot Studio agent with Planner connector tools can create, list and update tasks from natural-language requests, so users stop dragging cards by hand.
Fix group and plan IDs as custom values and write rich tool descriptions, because the orchestration model reads those descriptions to decide which tool to call.
Use Power Automate for deterministic, trigger-based workflows and Copilot Studio for interpretive requests, and govern connections, monitor analytics and respect licensing limits.
hook: Planner users waste time dragging, updating and re-dating tasks by hand. This episode shows Microsoft 365 and Power Platform makers how to build a Copilot Studio agent with Planner tools and publish it to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams, so plain-language requests turn into structured tasks.
